video_title: Cavs Practice | Kenny Atkinson Media Availability | 10.10.2026

quotes.speaker: Kenny Atkinson
quotes.summary_phrase: Kenny Atkinson on the drastic changes in offensive rebounding
quotes.excerpt: I think teams have realized that's a competitive advantage.
quotes.quote: I think teams have realized that's a competitive advantage. The possession game is a big part of winning in the NBA, so rebounding is obviously half of that and you got the turnovers. So you got those two things. I think teams have realized that's a competitive advantage.
quotes.social_post: Kenny Atkinson says offensive rebounding is a major competitive advantage in the modern NBA, noting that the possession game is a huge part of winning.

quotes.speaker: Kenny Atkinson
quotes.summary_phrase: Kenny Atkinson on the impact of shot volume differences
quotes.excerpt: Boston got 15 more shots up than us, and it's very simple math.
quotes.quote: The example would be the other night when Boston got 15 more shots up than us, and it's very simple math. They get 15 more shots, it's really hard to win if they get that many more shots.
quotes.social_post: Kenny Atkinson points to the math of shot volume, noting it is very hard to win when an opponent gets 15 more shots up than you.

quotes.speaker: Kenny Atkinson
quotes.summary_phrase: Kenny Atkinson on the impact of perimeter crashing
quotes.excerpt: It's the perimeter crashing. It's literally the sprint from the three-point line into the paint.
quotes.quote: The other thing is the perimeter crashing. It's literally the sprint from the three-point line into the paint. That's a different type of rebounding, box out, than maybe the scrum box out. We worked on it today. We got to be better. It's not just Celtics specific, I think it's league specific.
quotes.social_post: Kenny Atkinson says the Cavs are working on perimeter crashing, noting that sprinting from the three point line into the paint is a different type of box out.

quotes.speaker: Kenny Atkinson
quotes.summary_phrase: Kenny Atkinson on the need to meet opponents with force
quotes.excerpt: We have to go meet them with force, not let force come to us.
quotes.quote: We have to go meet them with force, not let force come to us. That makes like physics, right? We're kind of following the ball and they're coming at us and they're on our backs and they kind of hit us and then we're out of soul. So we have to go and meet them.
quotes.social_post: Kenny Atkinson says the Cavs need to meet opponents with force rather than letting force come to them to avoid getting pushed around on the glass.

quotes.speaker: Kenny Atkinson
quotes.summary_phrase: Kenny Atkinson on the difficulty of boxing out in space
quotes.excerpt: With the perimeter box outs, there's more space to go around the box out.
quotes.quote: With the perimeter box outs, there's more space to go around the box out if that makes sense. It's harder in space to box out, so we showed it on film obviously and then we got to keep working on our technique with that box out.
quotes.social_post: Kenny Atkinson explains that boxing out in space is difficult, which is why the team is focusing on technique to handle perimeter rebounding.

quotes.speaker: Kenny Atkinson
quotes.summary_phrase: Kenny Atkinson on the rebounding potential of new players
quotes.excerpt: I think Mario can be really good at it. I think Peyton can be really good at it.
quotes.quote: I think Mario can be really good at it. I think Peyton can be really good at it. We had one in the first or second possession where we got kicked it out and we got a three. It's just become part of the game, a big part of the game, and then related to the possession game.
quotes.social_post: Kenny Atkinson sees potential for Mario and Peyton to be strong rebounders as the team continues to emphasize the possession game.

quotes.speaker: Kenny Atkinson
quotes.summary_phrase: Kenny Atkinson on balancing freedom for offensive players
quotes.excerpt: I want to strike that balance, because he's a talented offensive player.
quotes.quote: I want to strike that balance, because he's a talented offensive player where I don't want him to be frozen and put him in a box. So I think right now I'm leaning more towards freedom, freedom to play, and I think that will help us observe him more and get to know his game more.
quotes.social_post: Kenny Atkinson says he is leaning toward giving his talented offensive players more freedom right now so he can better observe and understand their games.

quotes.speaker: Kenny Atkinson
quotes.summary_phrase: Kenny Atkinson on the importance of understanding officiating
quotes.excerpt: Another piece that's become more important is understanding how the game's being called.
quotes.quote: Another piece that's become more important is understanding how the game's being called, understanding and interpreting these new points of emphasis, educating the players. As coaches, I have to be educated. If I question a call, I want to be educated so I can speak on it correctly.
quotes.social_post: Kenny Atkinson emphasizes the importance of coaches and players staying educated on how the game is being called and understanding new points of emphasis.

quotes.speaker: Kenny Atkinson
quotes.summary_phrase: Kenny Atkinson on the communication growth of young players
quotes.excerpt: Jared and Evan, I don't know what they have taken a step up communication wise.
quotes.quote: Jared and Evan, I don't know what they have taken a step up communication wise and it's been a progressively they've gotten better at it. Jared particularly, I've noticed in the preseason, a lot louder, a lot more vocal, and Evan's getting better too.
quotes.social_post: Kenny Atkinson has noticed growth in communication from Jared and Evan, specifically noting that Jared has been much louder and more vocal during the preseason.
